whatThisIs: Practice-content map for Grade 6–8 WIDA Can Dos (Key Uses Edition). Each cell uses the official Can Do text. Pictures only when the Can Do names a visual, or when sequencing events requires a picture strip.

pictureRules.required: The Can Do names a photo, poster, chart, diagram, icon, illustrated text, graphic, or sequenced visuals. Supply exactly what picture.count and picture.type say.
pictureRules.not_needed: The Can Do is listening to talk, reading print, or producing speech/writing. Do not add a random library photo.
pictureRules.count: 1 = one scene. 2 = compare or cause/effect pair. 3 or 4 = a story or process in order (first → next → last). Never one photo when the skill is sequence.

canDo: Pointing to objects, people, or places based on short oral descriptions
Narrate.contentThatHelps: One still photo of a real scene with a person AND a place visible. Audio: 1–2 spoken sentences that describe location (who is where), not a long story.

picture.type: One photograph of a school or community scene (hallway, cafeteria, playground) with people and places large enough to tap.

canDo: Identifying familiar objects or places from oral statements
Inform.contentThatHelps: One still photo of familiar objects (desk items, cafeteria food, classroom). Audio names one object. Student finds it. Fact naming, not a plot.

picture.type: One photograph of a room with 3+ familiar objects (pencil, book, chair). Not a story sequence.

canDo: Matching instructional language, given orally, with visual representation (e.g., “Show me your schedule.”)
Identifying functions of content-related topics based on short oral statements reinforced visually (e.g., organisms in ecosystems)
Explain.contentThatHelps: One visual the oral line maps onto: a class schedule, a simple ecosystem poster, or a tool whose job is obvious. Audio is instruction or function (“Show me…”, “This is for sitting”), not only the object’s name.

picture.type: One schedule chart, one labeled ecosystem poster, OR one photo of a tool in use (chair, ruler, watering can). Not three story frames.

canDo: Signaling agreement or disagreement of short oral statements or questions
Identifying points of view (e.g., first or third person) from short statements
Argue.contentThatHelps: Short spoken claims. First Can Do: student agrees/disagrees. Second Can Do: audio uses I vs he/she — no picture required. Do not invent a story strip.

picture.type: None. If you add anything, it would only support agree/disagree about a visible object — that is extra, not the I/he skill.

canDo: Naming and briefly describing past community or school events using visual support (e.g., posters, photographs)
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student names a past event from the visual (who, what happened). 1–2 words or a short phrase.

picture.type: One photograph or poster of a past school/community event (field trip, assembly, game) already finished — not a blank classroom still-life.

canDo: Answering select Wh-questions
Inform.contentThatHelps: Spoken Who / What / Where. Student answers in 1–2 words. The Can Do does not name a picture.

picture.type: None. Do not add a random photo.

canDo: Comparing attributes of real-life objects with a partner
Showing how to solve real-world problems using symbols, numerals, graphs, or diagrams
Explain.contentThatHelps: Compare two real objects (size, color, amount) OR point at a number/symbol on a simple graph. Student says the difference or names the number.

picture.type: Two side-by-side photos of the same kind of object that differ in one attribute (two bottles, two leaves) OR one simple bar graph / number diagram — not a story strip.

canDo: Responding yes or no to short statements or questions related to a claim
Expressing personal points of view (in home language and English) in support of or against a claim
Argue.contentThatHelps: A short claim (school rule, food choice). Student says yes/no and I think… Home language allowed. No photo in the Can Do.

canDo: Identifying responses to Wh-questions in charts or illustrated text
Narrate.contentThatHelps: A chart with Who/Where labels OR illustrated text (pictures with 2–4 words). Student answers Wh from the chart/pictures, not from a paragraph.

picture.type: Either one two-column chart (Who / Where) OR a 3-panel illustrated strip of an event (girl → bus → school) with labels. Not one unlabeled photo.

canDo: Identifying icons in graphs, charts, and environmental print related to familiar topics
Inform.contentThatHelps: Icons and environmental print (exit, recycle, restroom) or a pictograph. Student names the icon. Not a story.

picture.type: Three separate icons or signs on one sheet (or three icon cards). Or one pictograph with 3 icon types. Not a photograph of a room.

canDo: Matching content-related objects, pictures, or media to words and phrases
Identifying social or academic topics highlighted in text
Explain.contentThatHelps: Match word to picture (first Can Do). Second Can Do is a 2–4 word caption: what is the topic? Use pictures only for the match skill.

picture.type: Three photos or drawings of content objects (leaf, rock, beaker) plus one printed word to match. Not a 3-panel story unless you are matching a process word.

canDo: Identifying words or phrases associated with topic choices
Classifying true from false short statements
Argue.contentThatHelps: Printed choices (soccer / basketball) or a 5-word true/false sentence. The Can Do is print, not pictures.

canDo: Producing labeled illustrations of conclusions reached in problem-solving with a partner
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student writes labels on a picture of a solved problem (amounts, more/less), not a narrative paragraph.

picture.type: One illustration of a simple math/science conclusion (two groups of blocks, a full vs empty container). Student adds labels. Not three story photos.

canDo: Reproducing words and phrases related to topics (e.g., including cognates)
Inform.contentThatHelps: A printed word bank of topic words (including cognates). Student copies the words. Can Do does not require a photo.

picture.type: None. Word bank on the page is enough.

canDo: Indicating relationships by drawing and labeling content-related pictures on familiar topics
Describing processes or cycles by labeling diagrams and graphs
Explain.contentThatHelps: Student labels a diagram or cycle (arrows, parts). Not a paragraph.

picture.type: One blank diagram or cycle with empty label lines (water cycle, plant parts, simple bar graph). Not a photo of a random classroom.

canDo: Generating words and phrases that represent opinions (e.g., "I think…")
Making lists of topic choices with peers
Argue.contentThatHelps: Sentence frame I think ___ and two printed topic choices. No picture.

canDo: Sequencing labeled visuals per oral directions
Identifying settings or time frames in narrative or informational scenarios read aloud
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Oral directions that put events in order. Student sequences labeled pictures of a STORY (trip, game). Second skill: audio of a story; student names setting (school/park) or time (morning/night).

picture.type: Three labeled stills of the SAME story in time order (pack bag → on the bus → at the zoo). Each picture is one moment. Do not use one photo.

canDo: Sequencing labeled visuals per oral directions
Identifying settings or time frames in narrative or informational scenarios read aloud
Inform.contentThatHelps: Same sequence skill, but pictures show a FACT process (recycle, wash hands, lab steps), not a plotted story. Audio is a report.

picture.type: Three labeled stills of one process in order (bottle → bin → truck). Not a story with characters.

canDo: Classifying content-related visuals per oral descriptions (e.g., environmental v. genetic factors)
Matching oral sentences of cause and effect to illustrations (e.g., weather or climate conditions)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Audio that sorts into two groups OR a because-sentence matched to pictures. Student classifies or matches cause → effect.

picture.type: For classify: two pictures that belong to two groups (rain cloud vs sun; plant vs animal). For cause/effect: two pictures — cause scene and effect scene (sun on puddle + dry ground). Not three story frames unless you are sequencing a process.

canDo: Identifying claims from a series of oral statements
Identifying evidence to support claims from charts and tables
Argue.contentThatHelps: Spoken claims. Second Can Do needs a chart the audio refers to (numbers that support the claim).

picture.type: One simple chart or table (tally or 3-column: cats 3, dogs 1). Not a photograph. First Can Do (hear the claim) is audio-only if you split items.

canDo: Stating main ideas or points of classroom conversations
Restating details of content-related topics (in home language and English) in small groups
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student restates the main point of something just heard or read (a mini story). 1–2 sentences. Can Do is talk, not tapping pictures.

canDo: Stating main ideas or points of classroom conversations
Restating details of content-related topics (in home language and English) in small groups
Inform.contentThatHelps: Student restates a FACT from a short lesson (one main idea + one detail). Home language OK.

canDo: Describing situations from modeled sentences
Connecting two content-related ideas that define "how" or "why"
Explain.contentThatHelps: A model sentence to copy/change. Student says how/why with because. No picture in the Can Do.

canDo: Answering simple questions related to claims
Stating evidence to support claims (in home language and English)
Argue.contentThatHelps: A claim plus Why? Student gives one reason. Print/speech only.

canDo: Sequencing illustrated text of narrative or informational events
Locating main ideas in a series of simple sentences
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Illustrated STORY events to put in order, plus simple sentences whose main idea they find. Sequence needs the pictures; main idea can be the same sentences under the pictures.

picture.type: Three illustrated panels of one story (each panel = one event with a short caption). Student orders them. Not one photo.

canDo: Sequencing illustrated text of narrative or informational events
Locating main ideas in a series of simple sentences
Inform.contentThatHelps: Illustrated FACT sequence (life cycle, how paper is made) plus simple informational sentences.

picture.type: Three illustrated panels of one process (seed → sprout → plant), each with a caption. Not a story with characters.

canDo: Comparing ideas on the same topic in a series of simple sentences
Identifying how content-related phenomena relate to one another in illustrated text or media
Explain.contentThatHelps: Two short texts on the same topic (compare) AND/OR illustrated text that shows how A relates to B.

picture.type: Two labeled diagrams or photos of the same topic that differ (mitosis vs meiosis; solid vs liquid). Each has 1–2 sentences. Not three story frames.

canDo: Distinguishing facts from opinions in text
Identifying features associated with content-related claims
Argue.contentThatHelps: Printed sentences: one fact, one opinion. Words like should, best, I think. No picture.

canDo: Completing sentences using word banks
Producing statements related to main ideas on familiar topics in home language and English
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Word bank + frames for a mini-story (First… Then…). The Can Do is completing sentences, not drawing.

picture.type: None. Printed word bank is the support WIDA names.

canDo: Completing sentences using word banks
Producing statements related to main ideas on familiar topics in home language and English
Inform.contentThatHelps: Word bank of topic words. Student writes a fact sentence.

canDo: Connecting short sentences
Comparing illustrated descriptions of content-related concepts (e.g., mitosis v. meiosis)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Student joins two short sentences (because/so) AND compares two illustrated science ideas.

picture.type: Two labeled illustrations of related concepts (two cell-division diagrams, or ice vs water). Student writes compare sentences. Not a 3-panel story.

canDo: Stating opinions using evaluative language related to content (e.g., "I agree. Metric is better.")
Connecting simple sentences to form content-related ideas
Argue.contentThatHelps: Frames: I agree/disagree because… Two linked sentences. Content opinion (metric, recess), not a photo.

canDo: Stating the next event in a series based on clues from narrative or informational oral texts
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Spoken story or oral report with a clear sequence. Stop before the last event. Student says/chooses what happens next. Clues are in the AUDIO.

picture.type: None. Do not add a picture strip unless you are also testing L2 sequence; this Can Do is oral clues.

canDo: Matching main ideas of familiar text read aloud to visuals
Inform.contentThatHelps: Familiar informational paragraph read aloud. Student picks the visual that matches the MAIN IDEA (not a tiny detail).

picture.type: Three different stills: one matches the main idea, two are related but wrong (detail or different topic). Example: recycling talk → (1) sorting bins (2) a single plastic bottle (3) a forest. Not three frames of one story.

canDo: Matching main ideas of familiar text read aloud with visuals
Showing differences between or among content-related phenomena described orally (e.g., descriptive statistics)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Spoken how/why or a comparison of two groups (numbers in the audio). Student matches main idea to a visual or says which group is larger.

picture.type: Two charts or two pictures that differ in the way the audio describes (week A vs week B rainfall bars). For main-idea match, three stills as in Inform. Not a story strip.

canDo: Illustrating claims or reasons from oral narratives
Identifying opposing perspectives from oral text (e.g., sides in wars, regimes, or revolutions)
Argue.contentThatHelps: Oral text with a claim+reason, or two opposing sides. Student identifies the claim or which side. Illustrating = showing they understood, not drawing.

canDo: Relating a series of events by expressing time in multiple tenses
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student tells events using past and another time (yesterday / now). 3–5 sentences. No picture in the Can Do.

canDo: Connecting ideas in content-related discourse using transitions
Inform.contentThatHelps: Student reports facts with first, also, for example. No picture.

canDo: Demonstrating how to conduct experiments, engage in processes, or solve problems with supports
Stating why events occur, phenomena exist, or some things happen
Explain.contentThatHelps: Spoken how-to (experiment steps) or why (because). Supports = sentence frame, not a photo.

canDo: Critiquing opposing claims
Evaluating the value of options in content-based situations
Argue.contentThatHelps: Two options or two claims. Student says which is weaker and why.

canDo: Connecting people to actions based on oral descriptions with details
Narrate.contentThatHelps: WIDA lists this under reading; practice as print: a paragraph where people do actions. Question: who did what. (If you follow the word oral strictly, that is listening — for reading, use a written description with the same skill.)

canDo: Identifying topic sentences, main ideas, and details in paragraphs
Inform.contentThatHelps: One informational paragraph: topic sentence + 2 details. Questions on each.

canDo: Illustrating relationships between main ideas and details in paragraphs
Sequencing steps or events to describe processes (e.g., solving math problems)
Explain.contentThatHelps: A how-to or process paragraph. Student matches detail to main idea or orders steps. Illustrating = showing the relationship, not drawing.

picture.type: None. Sequence the printed steps; do not add photos.

canDo: Identifying claims and the reasons for each claim
Identifying opposing points of view
Argue.contentThatHelps: A short opinion paragraph with because and another side (some people say).

canDo: Composing dialogues or blogs based on personal experiences
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student writes a short blog or two-person dialogue about something that happened to them.

canDo: Producing short paragraphs with main ideas and some details
Inform.contentThatHelps: Student writes one fact paragraph: main idea + 2 details.

canDo: Comparing and contrasting information, events, or characters
Producing descriptive paragraphs around a central idea
Explain.contentThatHelps: Write compare/contrast or one descriptive paragraph. Print prompt only.

canDo: Substantiating opinions with content-related examples and evidence
Providing feedback to peers on language used for claims and evidence
Argue.contentThatHelps: Opinion + a content example. Peer feedback is classroom talk; in solo practice, write claim + example only.

canDo: Identifying main ideas and details in oral discourse
Evaluating oral presentations of peers based on criteria for success
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Spoken narrative (story or personal recount). Questions: main idea vs detail. Second item: a peer-style oral presentation + a simple rubric (clear, complete).

canDo: Identifying main ideas and details in oral discourse
Evaluating oral presentations of peers based on criteria for success
Inform.contentThatHelps: Same skills on a spoken information report, not a plotted story.

canDo: Identifying relationships between people, ideas, or events in oral discourse
Matching complex oral descriptions to images, graphs, or formulas
Explain.contentThatHelps: Spoken how/why relationships. Second Can Do: audio describes a graph or formula; student picks the matching visual.

picture.type: Three graphs or diagrams that look similar (line up vs down vs flat). Audio describes one. Student selects. Not photos of people.

canDo: Matching evidence to claims in oral discourse
Formulating opinions based on evidence presented within oral discourse
Argue.contentThatHelps: Spoken argument: claim + evidence. Student matches evidence to claim or forms an opinion from the evidence given.

canDo: Connecting ideas with supporting details in a variety of oral venues
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Student tells a story or history with supporting details (not a fact list).

canDo: Paraphrasing and summarizing content-related ideas presented orally
Inform.contentThatHelps: Student hears content, then paraphrases. No picture.

canDo: Comparing content-related concepts
Connecting ideas with supporting details to show relationships (e.g., characters’ actions to their feelings)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Compare two concepts, or explain action → feeling. Speech only.

canDo: Connecting ideas with supporting details or evidence
Taking stances and summarizing ideas supporting them
Argue.contentThatHelps: Take a stance; summarize supporting ideas. No picture.

canDo: Ordering paragraphs in narrative and informational text
Identifying summaries of passages in a variety of genres
Narrate.contentThatHelps: A NARRATIVE with paragraphs out of order, or a story plus summary choices. (Informational ordering is the Inform cell.)

canDo: Ordering paragraphs in narrative and informational text
Identifying summaries of passages in a variety of genres
Inform.contentThatHelps: An INFORMATIONAL text with scrambled paragraphs, or pick the best summary of a report.

canDo: Matching content-related cause to effect in graphically-supported text
Highlighting text evidence that points to how systems function (e.g., different forms of government)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Cause-effect with a graphic. Second skill: print about how a system works; student highlights the how.

picture.type: One flowchart or cause-effect graphic in the text (bill becomes law; water cycle arrows). Plus the printed paragraph. Not three photos.

canDo: Identifying evidence to support analysis of what texts say (e.g., position papers)
Classifying pros and cons of claims and evidence presented within written texts
Argue.contentThatHelps: A short position paper. Mark evidence; sort pro vs con.

canDo: Reproducing a sequence of events or experiences using transitional words
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Write a sequence with first, then, after that, finally.

canDo: Producing content-related reports
Inform.contentThatHelps: Write a fact report, not a story.

canDo: Describing relationships between details or examples and supporting ideas
Connecting content-related themes or topics to main ideas
Explain.contentThatHelps: Write how details support an idea. No graphic required.

canDo: Crafting persuasive pieces (e.g., editorials) with a series of substantiated content-related claims
Composing scripts with protagonists and antagonists
Argue.contentThatHelps: Editorial with several claims, OR a short script of two opposing characters.

canDo: Sequencing a series of illustrated events from oral passages (e.g., historical recaps)
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Spoken historical recap. Student orders the illustrated events as heard.

picture.type: Four stills of one historical event in time (before battle → during → after → result), unlabeled or numbered out of order. Audio is the recap. Not one photo.

canDo: Categorizing details of content-related main ideas seen and heard in videos or other technologies
Inform.contentThatHelps: Video-style spoken report (or real clip if you have it). Student sorts details under two main ideas. Seeing = the video; if you only have audio, do not add random photos.

picture.type: None unless you play an actual short video. Do not fake video with unrelated library photos.

canDo: Carrying out a series of oral directions to construct mathematical or scientific models
Connecting details to main ideas based on extended oral discourse
Explain.contentThatHelps: Step-by-step oral directions to build a model, or extended how/why talk. Second skill is audio-only.

picture.type: None. The student constructs the model from directions; you do not show the finished picture first.

canDo: Establishing connections among claims, arguments, and supporting evidence within oral discourse
Comparing opposing points-of-view presented within oral discourse
Argue.contentThatHelps: Debate audio: two views, each with evidence. Student links claim–evidence or compares sides.

canDo: Tracing the evolution of literary characters, themes, and plots from different venues (e.g., digital text or video)
Narrate.contentThatHelps: After a short story (print). Student traces character/theme/plot change. Video is optional if you have a clip; do not add a random photo.

canDo: Producing oral multimedia, content-related reports based on research from multiple sources
Inform.contentThatHelps: Give two short sources in print. Student gives an oral report using both. Multimedia in WIDA means the student’s report; you do not need to show photos.

canDo: Giving demonstrations with step-by-step details (e.g., converting Fahrenheit to Celsius)
Evaluating the significance of events, people, or phenomena in oral presentations
Explain.contentThatHelps: Step-by-step demonstration (F to C) or why an event mattered. Speech only.

canDo: Engaging in debates on content-related topics with claims and counterclaims along with reasonable evidence
Defending points of view with specific claims
Argue.contentThatHelps: Debate prompt: claim, counterclaim, evidence. No picture.

canDo: Sequencing main ideas, events, and conclusions in narrative and informational text
Matching details of content-related topics to main ideas
Narrate.contentThatHelps: A NARRATIVE: sequence events/conclusions; match details to main ideas.

canDo: Sequencing main ideas, events, and conclusions in narrative and informational text
Matching details of content-related topics to main ideas
Inform.contentThatHelps: An INFORMATIONAL article: sequence conclusions; match details to headings.

canDo: Sorting grade-level text by highlighting elements of the genre (e.g., differentiating the "how" from the "why")
Sequencing events based on cause and effect (e.g., how machines operate)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Process text: label how vs why; order cause → effect. Print only.

canDo: Evaluating evidence presented in support of claims
Developing a stance in favor of or against claims presented within content-related text
Argue.contentThatHelps: Argumentative text. Judge evidence; take a stance.

canDo: Summarizing conclusions reached from steps in problem-solving or conducting experiments
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Given experiment/problem steps in print, write the conclusion as what was found, in order.

canDo: Producing research reports using multiple sources
Inform.contentThatHelps: Two printed sources in the prompt. Student writes a report using both.

canDo: Producing informational text around graphs and charts
Comparing content-related ideas from multiple sources in essays, reports, and narratives
Explain.contentThatHelps: Student writes about a graph/chart, or compares two printed sources.

picture.type: One graph or chart with a title and numbers (rainfall table, bar graph). Student writes from that graphic. Not a photograph.

canDo: Presenting opinions in persuasive essays or reports backed by content-related research
Justifying ideas using multiple sources
Argue.contentThatHelps: Two printed sources. Persuasive essay using both.

canDo: Identifying key ideas expressed orally
Identifying new information expressed by others
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Extended spoken narrative or discussion with two speakers. Student IDs key idea and what was new.

canDo: Identifying key ideas expressed orally
Identifying new information expressed by others
Inform.contentThatHelps: Same, on a factual oral exchange (not a story).

canDo: Evaluating main ideas and supporting details presented in diverse media and oral formats
Developing models from oral discourse and multimedia (e.g., YouTube videos)
Explain.contentThatHelps: Podcast-style explanation. Student evaluates main idea/details. Second Can Do: they build a model from the talk — you may show one diagram after, not as the question stem.

picture.type: None required. A YouTube clip is the WIDA example, not a still photo.

canDo: Evaluating the soundness of opposing claims presented orally
Identifying bias within claims in oral discourse
Argue.contentThatHelps: Two oral claims, one weaker or biased. Student judges soundness and bias.

canDo: Restating new information expressed by others in extended speech
Posing questions that elicit elaboration and responding to others’ questions and comments
Narrate.contentThatHelps: After a story, restate and ask a follow-up question. No picture.

canDo: Restating new information expressed by others in extended speech
Posing questions that elicit elaboration and responding to others’ questions and comments
Inform.contentThatHelps: After a fact talk, restate and ask a clarifying question.

canDo: Adapting speech to a variety of contexts and tasks (e.g., use of register)
Posing questions that connect several speakers’ ideas and responding to others’ ideas
Explain.contentThatHelps: Same idea, two registers (friend vs principal), or connect two speakers’ ideas.

canDo: Paraphrasing new information expressed by others and, when warranted, modifying views or positions
Making presentations with multimedia components to clarify claims and emphasize salient points
Argue.contentThatHelps: New fact may change the student’s claim. Multimedia is what the student would present — do not show a library photo as the task.

canDo: Evaluating how a central event is introduced, illustrated, and elaborated in text (e.g., through examples or anecdotes)
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Illustrated here means developed in writing (anecdotes, examples), not drawings. One event in a literary/historical passage.

picture.type: None. Illustrated = author’s examples in print.

canDo: Identifying a central idea of a text and how it is conveyed through particular details; summarizing text absent personal opinions or judgments
Inform.contentThatHelps: Informational text. Central idea, details, summary with no I think.

canDo: Comparing and contrasting information from experiments, simulations, videos, or multimedia sources with that of text on the same topics
Identifying factors that contribute to phenomena in explanations
Explain.contentThatHelps: Print text plus a second source described in print (what a simulation showed). Compare. Or list factors.

picture.type: None unless you embed a real video; do not add random photos.

canDo: Identifying specific evidence to support analyses of content area text
Distinguishing among facts, reasoned judgment, and speculation in text
Argue.contentThatHelps: Content argument. Label fact / judgment / speculation.

canDo: Conveying sequence, signaling shifts from one time frame to another, and showing the relationships among experiences and events
Narrate.contentThatHelps: Narrative with time shifts (years later) and how events connect.

canDo: Providing a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information presented
Inform.contentThatHelps: Report whose conclusion uses only the facts already written.

canDo: Determining two or more central ideas in text and tracing their development
Evaluating the interactions between individuals, events, and ideas in text (e.g., how ideas influence individuals or events and the converse)
Explain.contentThatHelps: WIDA lists these as writing Explain; they read like analysis. For practice: write a text that traces two ideas and how people/events affect each other. No picture.

canDo: Introducing claims and opposing claims, along with their associated reasons and evidence
Closing with concluding statements or paragraphs that support claims
Argue.contentThatHelps: Full argument: your claim, opposing claim, evidence, conclusion that matches your claim.
